note: The attacker-controlled, NUL-terminated JSON string (a truncated copy of the fuzzer input, parsed by monster_fuzzer's do_test -> Parser::ParseJson) is stored as the parser's source buffer; the tokenizer cursor_ is reset to walk this exact buffer.
Next() advances cursor_ one character at a time through the input buffer; here it has consumed all tokens of the JSON prefix up to the ':' after the field name.
The tokenizer sees the '+' sign character and enters the special '+/-inf' handling branch added for proto float defaults; cursor_ now points at the 'i' of "inf".

The three characters following the sign match "inf". The boundary check on the next line indexes cursor_[4] (off-by-one) instead of cursor_[3]: when the input ends with '+inf', cursor_[3] is the NUL terminator and cursor_[4] is one byte past it.

The off-by-one index reads cursor_[4], which lies one byte beyond the string's NUL terminator at cursor_[3] and is uninitialized memory; MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value at this read (src/idl_parser.cpp:495:47).
